name: The Last Ember

stars.name: Cinderwick
stars.notes: Slow-rotating neutron star with a 4.2-second period. Weak magnetar remnant—residual magnetic field still 10,000 times stronger than typical pulsars, though decaying steadily.

planets.name: Ashbone
planets.notes: Dense iron-nickel remnant, likely the exposed core of a larger world stripped by the supernova. Surface is magnetically scarred with patterns that shift over decades.

planets.name: The Reliquary
planets.notes: Cold, radiation-blasted world. Deep radar scans reveal a network of sealed chambers beneath the southern polar region, contents unknown. Entry attempts have failed due to material hardness exceeding known alloys.

anomalies.name: The Sealed Vaults
anomalies.location: Beneath the southern pole of The Reliquary
anomalies.notes: Network of chambers detected by deep radar, sealed behind walls of an unidentified crystalline-metallic composite. Estimated age exceeds 3 billion years. No drilling or cutting technology has successfully breached the outer layer.

asteroid_belts.name: Pyre Ring
asteroid_belts.location: Outer system, beyond The Reliquary's orbit
asteroid_belts.notes: Heavily irradiated metallic debris. Contains isotope ratios consistent with supernova nucleosynthesis—raw material from the death of the original star.

stations.name: Vigil Point
stations.notes: Minimal research outpost maintained by the Archaeo-Xenological Society. Crew rotates annually. Focused entirely on attempts to understand or breach the Sealed Vaults.

faction_control.notes: The Society holds a research claim recognized by the Exploration Guild. No other faction has expressed interest in contesting it.

history: Discovered in 2461 during a neutron star survey. Initial classification as a dead system was revised when deep radar aboard the survey vessel detected the subsurface chambers on The Reliquary.

The Archaeo-Xenological Society established Vigil Point in 2488, beginning what would become the longest continuous study of a pre-human artifact site in known space. Forty years of effort have produced extensive mapping of the vault network but zero penetration.
In 2519, a brief burst of coherent radiation was detected emanating from within the vaults—the only indication that something inside may still be active. The event has not repeated.
description: The Last Ember is a graveyard lit by the faintest of lanterns. Cinderwick, the neutron star at its heart, pulses once every 4.2 seconds—a slow, tired heartbeat for a stellar corpse. Two worlds remain in orbit: Ashbone, a magnetically tortured iron ball, and The Reliquary, a cold world with a secret buried deep beneath its southern pole. The Pyre Ring encircles the outer system like a wreath of metallic ash, the scattered remains of worlds that did not survive their star's death.

The Sealed Vaults are what draw the few visitors this system receives. Something built chambers beneath The Reliquary's surface and sealed them with a material that laughs at modern cutting tools. Whatever waits inside has been waiting for over three billion years—longer than multicellular life has existed on Earth. The single burst of radiation detected in 2519 suggests that the wait is not passive; something within those vaults still functions, still responds, still keeps its own counsel.

The twelve researchers at Vigil Point carry on their work with the quiet persistence of people who know they may never succeed. Each year's crew inherits the same problem and the same unyielding walls. The vaults do not open. The neutron star does not explain. And somewhere beneath kilometers of frozen rock, behind a material that should not exist, something ancient continues to do whatever it was built to do.
